Objective We recently reported successful treatment of a child with febrile infection‐related epilepsy syndrome (FIRES), a subtype of new onset refractory status epilepticus, with the recombinant interleukin‐1 (IL1) receptor antagonist (IL1RA) anakinra. On this basis, we tested whether endogenous IL1RA production or function is deficient in FIRES patients. Methods Levels of IL1β and IL1RA were measured in serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). The inhibitory activity of endogenous IL1RA was assessed using a cell‐based reporter assay. IL1RN gene variants were identified by sequencing. Expression levels for the secreted and intracellular isoforms of IL1RA were measured in patient and control cells by real‐time polymerase chain reaction. Results Levels of endogenous IL1RA and IL1β were elevated in the serum and CSF of patients with FIRES (n = 7) relative to healthy controls (n = 10). Serum from FIRES patients drove IL1R signaling activity and potentiated IL1R signaling in response to exogenous IL1β in a cell‐based reporter assay. Functional assessment of endogenous IL1RA activity in 3 FIRES patients revealed attenuated inhibition of IL1R signaling. Sequencing of IL1RN in our index patient revealed multiple variants. This was accompanied by reduced expression of intracellular but not secreted isoforms of IL1RA in the patient's peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Interpretation Our findings suggest that FIRES is associated with reduced expression of intracellular IL1RA isoforms and a functional deficiency in IL1RA inhibitory activity. These observations may provide insight into disease pathogenesis for FIRES and other inflammatory seizure disorders and may provide a valuable biomarker for therapeutic decision‐making. Ann Neurol 2019;85:526–537 Center for Multiple Sclerosis and Autoimmune Neurology Mayo Clinic Center for Regenerative Medicine Child Neurology Foundation Research 93346001 NIH National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke NS064571 source-schema-version-number 2.0 component-id ana25439 cover-date April 2019 details-of-publishers-convertor Converter:WILEY_ML3GV2_TO_NLMPMC version:5.6.2.1 mode:remove_FC converted:01.05.2019 Febrile infection‐related epilepsy syndrome (FIRES), 1 a subtype of new onset refractory status epilepticus (SE), 2 is a rare seizure disorder defined by the occurrence of refractory SE that lacks a structural, toxic, or metabolic cause starting between 2 weeks and 24 hours after febrile illness, with or without fever at the onset of SE. 3 , 4 Most FIRES patients are treated with antiseizure drugs, ketogenic diet, 5 immunomodulatory therapies, and/or medically induced coma, 6 with low overall therapeutic efficacy rates. 7 , 8 The majority of FIRES cases have poor outcomes, including development of refractory focal epilepsy, cognitive decline, brain atrophy, vegetative state, and death. 9 , 10 In a recent study, 12% of patients died during the acute phase of the disease, and 93% of survivors developed refractory epilepsy, with the majority showing significant cognitive impairment. 8 Magnetic resonance imaging in chronic cases revealed cortical and hippocampal atrophy, 11 and brain biopsies indicated gliosis without overt immune cell infiltration. Investigations into genetic or infectious causes have generally been negative. 12 These findings emphasize how little is known regarding FIRES etiology and underscore the possibility of multiple distinct etiologies. 13 Anakinra is a recombinant form of the endogenous interleukin‐1 receptor antagonist (rIL1RA). We recently reported the successful use of anakinra across 3 separate treatment epochs in a developmentally normal 32‐month‐old girl who progressed to super‐refractory SE secondary to FIRES following banal febrile respiratory infection. 14 Based on 12‐month follow‐up clinical examination, her motor, verbal, and social development were within normal limits for her age, suggesting a remarkable neuroprotective potential of anakinra treatment in FIRES. IL1R signaling is implicated in febrile seizures 15 and epileptogenesis, 16 and single dose IL1RA treatment has previously been shown to reduce spike frequency in animal models of SE. 17 Several lines of evidence suggest that blocking IL1R signaling in the brain during severe acute inflammatory states may be beneficial. In a rodent model of sepsis, IL1RA administration blocked the proconvulsant effect of intraperitoneal injection with lipopolysaccharide. 18 IL1R signaling blockade was also found to reduce blood–brain barrier disruption, inflammation, and forebrain neuron loss in rat models of SE, 17 , 19 and to prevent progression in models of acquired epilepsy. 20 Likewise, transgenic overexpression of IL1RA in astrocytes resulted in potent antiseizure effects. 21 More recently, rIL1RA was found to prevent seizure sensitization when acutely administered in a mouse model of post‐traumatic epilepsy, 22 and rIL1RA therapy successfully halted seizures in a child with persistent systemic inflammation and epilepsy unresponsive to multiple antiseizure drugs. 23 The mechanism of IL1RA‐mediated antiseizure activity is unclear and has not been studied in the context of FIRES. Surprisingly, we found that FIRES patients had elevated levels of endogenous IL1RA in serum (n = 5) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF; n = 7) prior to the initiation of anakinra treatment. Given this unexpected elevation, coupled to the anakinra responsiveness of our index case, we hypothesized that the endogenous IL1RA in these subjects is functionally compromised. To test this hypothesis, we established a cell‐based reporter assay to measure IL1RA function in serum and CSF collected from healthy controls (HCs), FIRES patients, and patients with other seizure disorders.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigates the functional deficiency of endogenous interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (IL1RA) in Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) patients, a subtype of new-onset refractory status epilepticus. It characterizes inflammatory markers, including IL1RA, inflammatory cytokines (IL1β, IL6, TNF-α), chemokines (CXCL10, IL8), and IL1RN gene variants in serum, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from FIRES patients, healthy controls, and other epilepsy conditions (Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus, Epilepsy with Electrical Status Epilepticus during Slow-wave Sleep, Medically Refractory Epilepsy). Key findings include elevated but functionally deficient endogenous IL1RA (particularly in CSF), increased IL1R signaling activity resistant to antagonism, reduced expression of intracellular IL1RN isoforms in PBMCs, and the presence of noncoding IL1RN gene polymorphisms, all contributing to impaired IL1R signaling inhibition in FIRES.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study primarily focused on biomarker characterization rather than dose-response comparisons for Anakinra. However, Anakinra therapy was initiated in some FIRES patients, and biomarker levels were measured before and after its administration, demonstrating its therapeutic effect in restoring IL1R signaling inhibition. Specific in-vivo dose and duration details were not extensively reported, though in vitro experiments used 65pM rIL1RA for inhibition.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated in serum and CSF of FIRES patients (n=7) relative to healthy controls (n=10). Elevated in some patients with either FIRES or Medically Refractory Epilepsy (MRE), and in all FIRES patients and most MRE patients in CSF. Significant increases in both serum and CSF in FIRES patients, often just above detection limits, with HEK-Blue IL1R cell-based assay proving more sensitive than ELISA and cytometric bead assays.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Mediates inflammation and epileptogenesis through IL1R signaling; IL1R agonist, inflammatory cytokine.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) and Medically Refractory Epilepsy (MRE) patients before anakinra treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated levels indicate inflammatory activity and, in conjunction with IL1RA deficiency, may provide insight into disease pathogenesis for FIRES, representing a target for anti-inflammatory therapy.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated in serum (n=5) and CSF (n=7) of FIRES patients relative to healthy controls (n=10) prior to anakinra treatment. Marginally elevated in FIRES serum compared to HCs, not differing from MRE patients but significantly different from HCs. Strongly elevated in FIRES CSF compared to Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH) CSF and other MRE patients, often exceeding serum levels. Significantly elevated in serum and CSF of the index FIRES patient, with CSF levels more elevated than serum, relative to controls.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Inhibits IL1R signaling, which is involved in inflammation and epileptogenesis; endogenous antagonist of IL1R signaling, principle component of negative feedback in the IL1R cascade, suggests localized CNS production.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) patients prior to anakinra treatment, compared to healthy controls (HC), normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH), and other medically refractory epilepsy (MRE) patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Despite elevated protein levels, a functional deficiency is observed, indicating disease pathogenesis. Elevated CSF levels represent a consistent biomarker for FIRES, suggesting a potential functional deficiency despite high concentrations. This can act as an IL1R antagonist and may represent a normal acute response or a chronic failure to terminate ongoing IL1R signaling.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Inhibitory Activity (functional assessment via cell-based reporter assay)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Attenuated inhibition of IL1R signaling observed in 3 FIRES patients. Serum from FIRES patients also drove and potentiated IL1R signaling in response to exogenous IL1β. CSF contained 65pM endogenous IL1RA (~1 ng/ml) but did not inhibit IL1R signaling in response to 32 pg/ml IL1β, in contrast to 65pM recombinant IL1RA which inhibited IL1R signaling in dialyzed NPH CSF.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Inhibition of IL1R signaling, involved in inflammation and epileptogenesis; antagonizes IL1R signaling to terminate inflammatory responses.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) prior to anakinra therapy (dysfunctional IL1RA).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Functional deficiency in IL1RA inhibitory activity indicates disease pathogenesis and is a valuable biomarker for therapeutic decision-making in FIRES; provides direct mechanistic support for the therapeutic efficacy of anakinra despite elevated protein levels.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Measured at 24 ng/ml IL1RA and robustly suppressed IL1R signaling in response to 32 pg/ml IL1β.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Antagonizes IL1R signaling to terminate inflammatory responses.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: FIRES patient after initiation of anakinra therapy.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Demonstrates that anakinra therapy effectively restores IL1R signaling inhibition, correlating with patient clinical improvement (seizure termination).

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein Level (ELISA) and Gene Transcript Expression Level (real-time polymerase chain reaction)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly reduced protein levels in FIRES patient PBMCs compared to healthy controls, corresponding to a 21-fold decrease in total IL1RN mRNA levels. Reduced expression of intracellular IL1RA isoforms was observed in the index patient's PBMCs.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulates IL1R signaling internally; intracellular forms of IL1RA can be secreted in response to specific triggers and serve as acute response molecules to antagonize IL1R signaling.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) in the index patient, comparing PBMCs to healthy controls.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Reduced and aberrant expression of intracellular IL1RA contributes to the observed impairment in inhibitory function and the overall functional deficiency in IL1RA in FIRES pathogenesis.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Gene Transcript Expression Level (real-time polymerase chain reaction)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No reduced expression of secreted IL1RA isoforms in the index patient's peripheral blood mononuclear cells.

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) in the index patient.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: The lack of change in secreted isoforms, in contrast to reduced intracellular isoforms, helps characterize the specific nature of IL1RA deficiency in FIRES pathogenesis.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 21-fold decrease in untreated FIRES PBMCs relative to controls.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a profound transcriptional dysregulation of the IL1RN gene, contributing to the functional deficit in IL1RA in FIRES patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Profound decrease in expression of a dominant intracellular IL1RN isoform, contributing significantly to the overall functional deficit in IL1RA in FIRES patients.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Encodes secreted isoform 1 (sIL1RA I), a minor IL1RN transcript in healthy individuals.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: FIRES patient PBMCs compared to healthy control PBMCs.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Proportional increase is likely a consequence of the severe reduction in dominant intracellular isoforms, not an indicator of improved IL1RA function.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No variants detected in translated coding sequences. Several novel and previously reported variants found in intronic sequences, and a silent mutation in exon 6. Specifically, 15 polymorphisms between exons 2 and 3, including duplication of TTC at 2:113121042 and substitutions at 2:113121134 (C to A) and 2:113121138 (A to G).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Genetic sequence encoding IL1RA, where polymorphisms can influence gene expression, splicing, and protein function.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Intronic mutations are associated with possible splicing changes (e.g., breakage of exonic splicing silencer elements, creation of exonic splicing enhancers, activation of cryptic intronic acceptor sites) that could alter IL1RN isoform expression and lead to functional IL1RA deficiency in FIRES.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased IL1R activity relative to that induced by HC or MRE serum (MRE did not differ from HCs). FIRES and Epilepsy with Electrical Status Epilepticus during Slow-wave Sleep (ESES) patient serum synergized with exogenous IL1β (32 pg/ml) to induce even more IL1R activity. The amount of IL1R signaling activity induced by serum was not completely suppressed by the addition of exogenous IL1RA in samples from FIRES and ESES patients, whereas activity was mostly suppressed in HC and MRE samples.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Mediates inflammatory responses, cellular signaling cascade.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: FIRES and ESES patient serum, compared to HC and MRE serum.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates dysregulated or exaggerated inflammatory signaling in FIRES and ESES; suggests resistance to IL1RA antagonism; implies presence of other serum factors driving IL1R activity or an undetected IL1β reservoir.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Typically <1 pg/ml, which is far below the >100 pg/ml required to induce a response in HEK-Blue IL1R cells.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Not a significant contributor to IL1R signaling in this context due to very low concentrations.
